summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, chronic diastolic heart failure, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, and prior venous thromboembolism was admitted after presenting with dizziness, palpitations, and hypotension. She had recently had her furosemide dose doubled, leading to hypovolemia and sinus tachycardia. Initial labs showed subtherapeutic INR (1.9), prompting bridging with Lovenox until therapeutic range was achieved. IV fluids and reinitiation of metoprolol helped stabilize her heart rate and blood pressure. Her polymyositis remained stable, and metformin was held during admission. Pulmonary vascular congestion was noted on chest X-ray but was managed with diuretic adjustment. She was discharged back to an extended care facility on her prior medications with furosemide reduced to 40 mg BID and instructions to monitor weight and INR.
problems: Other diuretics causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
